title: Regrets about quitting music after the Army
summary: After four years in a service band and marriage, he took a steady job in Chicago and stopped playing, wishing to return.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Well we're about out of tape here. Is there any other thing you'd like to add about your own life or anything else before we quit?
Well the only thing about my, I just was sorry that I just stopped playing, period. Because I don't think there's anything else that I would rather do than play.
Well maybe there's still a chance.

But the thing about it, when I came out of the Army I was pretty sharp I'd say this because I had played with the service band for four years. But I also came out with the wife. So therefore I had to sort of look out for myself and the wife and the way the country was in such a condition. And the trend had deviated from the big bands to the small combinations and it just appeared to be a dogfight for recognition because the field had gotten so crowded. And musicians were just plentiful around Chicago, plentiful. And so I decided maybe I'd better go on back to the job that I had because I knew that I could make an honest living and a fairly decent living. And I said well maybe I would practice from time to time just to sort of keep up my instrument. And then I had joined the Army Reserve Force and I was a part of that for about two years. About four years but we didn't seem to get too much out of it because then they started reverting everything to military personnel and just taking some away from the music end of it you know. So therefore they-
Well I hope you do get back to it sometime again because-

Yes. I'd like to get back because I don't think there's anything I would much rather do than play music. Because I enjoyed every bit of it. Very much so even though I didn't make much money but I had a whole lot of fun. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah.
